The live citation binds the actual retained result, witness identity, producer, ProgramIndex identity, exact prepared mapping/document scope, and exact fact owner/key. Substituted witness/address objects, foreign source/documents and copied results are refused.

ReaderProjectionClaimProof must share the original result/index/document when present. Semantic source spans and proof strength are unchanged; removing semantic qualification leaves valid placement independent, as required by R4.

Finite migrated slot/reader guards deny legacy class-span fallback when the citation is empty, missing or erased. This prevents a shared normalization implementation from placing unrelated embedding/final norms.
Config-object no_mapping inputs remain declared and unqualified without a citation; conversion to_dict is not used as checkpoint authority. Losing a previously sealed mapping is rejected.
Ordinary fact serialization omits the live receipt. asdict/deepcopy yields only portable diagnostic addresses; reconstructed dicts are rejected by native fact validation and by the placement join.

Explicit canonical block source_instance_path remains an independent positive placement authority even when a migrated fact has no live receipt and no semantic qualification. Its unstamped finding remains separate.
The fact-claim cache change avoids eager setdefault evaluation and does not alter keys or matched claims.
limitations: Independent source review only; reviewer ran no tests, models, imports of product modules, or actual S7 generation.
Root must run all new placement poisons, existing norm/declaration/reconciliation controls, supported real object-input checks, and actual affected-model/full-matrix delta audit.
Other fact readers retain explicitly unmigrated legacy span placement. This bounded fix does not certify that legacy join.

External normalization primitives have no internal target in this bounded rail; they retain semantic proof but cannot recover placement from caller/class fallback. Any count change must be enumerated, never hidden or self-approved.
